# Final comparison notes

The user supplied Approach B historical figures and explicitly instructed their inclusion. They are authoritative for this revision: March 15: 294 households, actual 11,163.59 kWh, forecast 9,752.96 kWh, -12.64%; September 5: 374, 5,047.35, 7,154.21, +41.74%; February 27: 371, 11,256.81, 11,213.98, -0.38%. Approach B final February forecast is the updated 410-household result: 12,011.58 kWh. The old 372-only portfolio total is not used.

Each historical table row uses that approach's own measured household support. A counts are 368/381/374, B counts 294/374/371. Actual totals consequently differ. These are parallel evaluations, not an identical-support comparison or a controlled performance ranking. B exact historical household prediction sets remain unavailable. A saved predictions and actuals were joined one-to-one on household ID and UTC timestamp. Missing actuals were not converted to zero.

Sources: user-provided B historical results; latest sibling Masha Python implementation and updated 410-household Word description; existing A model locks, fit summaries, historical prediction and label parquet files, February household CSV, uncertainty evaluation, weather evaluation and metric CSVs. Source hashes and exact reconstructed household rosters follow.

Daily MWh is sum of 15-minute kWh divided by 1,000. Signed percentage error is 100*(forecast-actual)/actual. Absolute error is abs(forecast-actual). User percentages agree with computation to two decimals. Rounded Word/Markdown values are generated from the same figures as the CSVs. A's full-year metrics are not presented as equivalent to B's three-day evaluation.

A main model fitted on 392 households, auxiliary cold model on 352 established households. B final Ridge fitting uses 372; remaining forecasts route to 11 previous-week profiles, 23 historical profiles, 4 portfolio imputations. These routing counts were independently reconstructed from data without model fitting. Both February forecasts cover all 410. A historical active roster counts are 402/406/410, distinct from measured scoring sets.

A daily P10/P50/P90 are empirical portfolio quantiles: 10.47020838018431 / 12.38117163410992 / 14.681127018351994 MWh. Its point is 13.014908665757588 MWh. B conformal intervals concern Ridge household quarter-hours, not a daily full-portfolio bound. None is invented. February actual demand is absent, so no error is calculated. No ensemble, retraining, retuning or test-based selection occurred. All existing model/source hashes remain unchanged.

Information cutoffs differ: A issues 11:00 local the preceding day, while B uses the complete preceding UTC day. A behavioural calendar is Europe/Berlin, B's UTC. Both target grids use 96 UTC slots. These conditions and different observed supports are stated as limits on comparisons. PV/EV inputs were evaluated and included in A's cold model, not its locked main model. Direct PV generation was not measured.

The report omits process diagnostics as requested by the user. The supplied B Python source's non-breaking spaces and unavailable saved numerical output files remain reproducibility limitations, not additional claims in the submission text. The revised document is a descriptive comparison using supplied values; historical common-support validity has not been established.
